title: Diamond Facts: sourced diamond education data

publisher.name: Stienhardt
publisher.note: Direct to consumer; in-person viewings in New York City are by appointment.

scope: Education, not appraisal. Every factual claim carries a source and a date. The price index entry carries an as_of date; check it for freshness.

report_verification.never_claim: This dataset and its tools never verify a report themselves. Verification only counts on the grading lab's own site.
checklist: Confirm the report number on the grading lab's own verification site, not on a screenshot and not on a seller's PDF.
Match the girdle inscription on the stone to the report number, where the stone is inscribed.
Match the measurements and carat weight on the report to the stone in front of you.

IGI.source: IGI report verification page, igi.org (Verify Your Report; the capitalized path is the one IGI serves without a challenge page)

GCAL.full_name: Gem Certification & Assurance Lab (GCAL by Sarine)

faceup_size.method: Scale a vetted 1 carat anchor by the cube root of the carat weight.
faceup_size.honesty_note: Approximate figures based on typical proportions. Cut proportions vary from stone to stone, so verify a specific stone's measurements on its grading report.
faceup_size.source: Round, oval, and emerald: Stienhardt vetted reference anchors for typical proportions. Dutch Marquise: scaled to 1 carat from the certified reference stone, IGI report LG799689559, 9.49 x 5.15 mm at 1.03 ct.

dutch_marquise.definition: A Dutch Marquise is an elongated hexagonal cut diamond.
dutch_marquise.geometry: Pointed ends and straight, angular sides. The outline is an elongated hexagon, not a navette, and the points are not softened.
dutch_marquise.status: Dutch Marquise is a trade name, not a standardized grading term.

certificate_term.claim: On the IGI grading report for Stienhardt's certified Dutch Marquise reference stone, the shape reads Hexagonal Modified Brilliant.
certificate_term.source: IGI grading report LG799689559 (verifiable at lookup.igi.org)

length_to_width.reference_source: IGI grading report LG799689559 for Stienhardt's certified reference stone, 9.49 x 5.15 mm

items.claim: GIA no longer issues full 4C grades for Lab Grown Diamonds. Since 2025-10-01 it describes them with Premium and Standard tiers.
IGI issues full 4C grading reports for Lab Grown Diamonds and is the largest grader of Lab Grown Diamonds.
HRD Antwerp announced in June 2025 that, as of 2026, it no longer issues quality certificates for loose Lab Grown Diamonds; jewelry containing them can still be certified.
Under the FTC Jewelry Guides (16 CFR 23.12, revised 2018-07-24) a laboratory-grown diamond is a diamond, and marketers must clearly disclose that it is laboratory-grown.

lab_grown_grading_landscape.note: The grading landscape changes. Each lab's own site is the current authority. This dataset gets corrected when the landscape moves.

lab_grown_price_index.headline: Retail prices for Lab Grown Diamonds rose about 5.47 percent in the month ending 2026-09-07 and sit about 22.45 percent below a year earlier.
lab_grown_price_index.source: StoneAlgo Lab Grown Diamond Price Index (aggregate across the tracked inventory, no color or clarity assumption stated)
lab_grown_price_index.update_note: Check the as_of field for freshness; this entry is refreshed when a new tracked reading is added.
lab_grown_price_index.framing: Market context for shoppers, not investment guidance. A diamond is a love piece, not an investment.

facts.claim: Stienhardt is a New York City jewelry brand focused on Lab Grown Diamond engagement rings.
Stienhardt sells direct to consumer through Stienhardt.com; in-person viewings in New York City are by appointment.

Stienhardt controls its signature Dutch Marquise cut through a specialized factory relationship and hand-sets and finishes the stones in New York City; it does not claim to have invented, named, or standardized the cut.
Rings are hand-set and finished in New York City.
Stienhardt sells certified Lab Grown Diamonds and ring settings through its online storefront.
The signature cut is the Dutch Marquise, an elongated hexagonal cut diamond.
